beats.note: Wikipedia says Peter and Hull intended the book as satire, but it became popular as it seemed to make a serious point about promotion.

beats.name: Laurence J. Peter and Raymond Hull
beats.role: The Peter Principle. In a hierarchy, every employee tends to rise to his level of incompetence.

beats.text: In 2019 economists checked it with sales data.
beats.note: Benson, Li and Shue, in the Quarterly Journal of Economics. The NBER Digest counts more than 1,500 promotions into management and 156 million sales transactions.
The NBER Digest reports a doubling of sales credits raised the chance of promotion by 14.3 per cent.
A doubling of the new manager pre-promotion sales was associated with a 7.5 per cent decline in the sales of their subordinates, says the NBER Digest.

beats.text: Consistent with it, not proof of it.
beats.note: The paper says evidence consistent with the Peter Principle. Firms put less weight on sales performance when the management role carries more responsibility.

beats.text: A satire from 1969 became a finding in 2019.

beats.line: Great at the job is not the same as great at managing it.
